name: AASHTO Green Book 2018 (metric) - Cross-section elements
source: AASHTO, A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, 7th ed. (2018), Chapter 3 (superelevation, widening) and Chapter 4 (cross-section elements). Values were checked against the Green Book text available to the author (2001 edition, same values); 2018 table numbers are cited by section.
advisory: Defaults and advisory checks only; any value can be used and a value outside a range is reported, never blocked.

references.lane_width: Section 4.3 (2.7-3.6 m; 3.6 m predominant on high-type highways)
references.shoulder_width: Section 4.4.2 (0.6-3.6 m; 3.0 m normal on high-type facilities)
references.shoulder_crossfall: Section 4.4.3 (paved 2-6 %, gravel 4-6 %, turf 6-8 %; max 8 % algebraic difference at the high side)
references.curbs: Section 4.7 (vertical 150-200 mm; sloping max 150 mm with a 1V:1H to 1V:2H face)
references.lanes_rotated: Table 3-16 adjustment factor bw = (1 + 0.5 (n1 - 1)) / n1 (2001: Exhibit 3-28)
references.widening: Section 3.3.10, Table 3-26 (2001: Exhibit 3-51), WB-15 design vehicle; minimum 0.6 m, smaller values disregarded
references.slopes: Section 4.8 and Roadside Design Guide: 1V:4H or flatter recoverable, 1V:3H traversable

lane.width.note: 3.6 m desirable; 3.3 m acceptable in urban areas; 3.0 m on low-speed facilities; 2.7 m on low-volume roads.

lane.crossfall.note: High-type surfaces; up to 2.5 % with three or more lanes in one direction; 4 % maximum.

shoulder.crossfall.note: Paved 2-6 %; gravel or crushed rock 4-6 %; turf 6-8 %.

shoulder.breakover.note: Algebraic difference between travelled way and shoulder at the high side.

fill.slope.note: 1V:4H or flatter recoverable; 1V:3H traversable but non-recoverable.

widening.ref: Table 3-26 (2001 Exhibit 3-51), roadway width 7.2 m, WB-15
widening.rule: A radius at or below the row's value (and above the previous row's) gets that row's widening; values below the minimum are disregarded.

superelevation.runoff_on_tangent_ref: Section 3.3.8: 60-80 % of the runoff on the tangent without spirals (two-thirds used)
superelevation.shoulder_rule_ref: Section 4.4.3 (8 % maximum algebraic difference at the high side)

slope_bands.ref: Section 4.8 (single slope; use the editor's bands for height-dependent slopes)

side_drains.ref: Section 4.8 roadside channels (shapes; size from hydraulics)

Carriageway.ref: Example only - enter the pavement design

Urban street with curbs.ref: Sections 4.3, 4.7, 4.17: 3.3 m lanes, vertical curb, 1.5 m sidewalk

Four-lane divided highway.ref: Sections 4.3, 4.4, 4.11: 3.6 m lanes, 3.0 m outside and 1.2 m inside shoulders

unsourced: 2018 table numbers (3-15, 3-16, 3-26) are cited from the 2018 edition's arrangement; the values were checked in the 2001 text (Exhibits 3-27, 3-28, 3-51). Confirm against the 2018 book.
Widening for radii below 150 m (7.2 m roadway) is not included: the scanned table layout is ambiguous.
